newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil INPC inflation rises 0.81 pct in Jan - IBGE.
newsitem.headline: Brazil INPC inflation rises 0.81 pct in Jan - IBGE.

text.p: Brazilian inflation in January as measured by the National Consumer Price Index (INPC) was 0.81 percent, up from 0.33 percent in December 1996, the government's National Statistics Institute (IBGE) said.
The IBGE also said its Wider Consumer Price Index (IPCA) registered inflation of 1.18 percent in January, up from 0.47 percent in the previous month.
The INPC is based on the spending of families earning up to eight times the minimum wage of 112 reais, while the IPCA measures spending of families earning up to 40 times the minimum wage.
The increase in the INPC inflation index was mostly due to a 9.98 percent increase in fuel prices, IBGE said in a statement.
Of the 11 geographical areas, Rio de Janeiro showed the highest inflation rate of 1.22 percent. The lowest level was registered in Belem, an increase of just 0.06 percent.
